title: Constant scalar restriction preserves tensor, total complexes and K-flat localization
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], with exact abelian sheafification and the sheafified tensor structures [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $R=\underline B$ its constant ring sheaf, and $\iota:B^{\mathrm{pre}}\to R$ its sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $C_B:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ be restriction to constant scalar sections [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], with the canonical inverse extending scalar actions locally. It is an additive exact symmetric monoidal equivalence for the ordinary sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and sheafified objectwise $\otimes_B$, with natural comparisons
$$C_B(M\otimes_R N)\cong C_B(M)\otimes_B C_B(N),\qquad C_B(R)\cong\underline B.$$
Both tensor maps send each local pure tensor to the same pure tensor, and the unit comparison sends the image of each constant scalar to itself. These maps commute with associators, unitors and symmetry. Termwise they give natural isomorphisms of signed direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and preserve and reflect flatness and K-flatness. Here flatness means exactness of tensor with the object, and K-flatness means acyclicity after total tensor with every acyclic complex; equivalently both total tensor functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For ordinary unbounded K-flat derived tensors the induced equivalence $D(C_B)$ has the coherent tensor comparison computed by those total-complex maps on corresponding K-flat resolutions. No finiteness, nonzero-ring, enough-points or terminal-object hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor; agent-written constant-presheaf specialization with coherent total-complex and K-flat descent, serving original coefficient-comparison steps 3, 5-6.

proof.text: Write $E$ for action extension in [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]. Its statement identifies its inverse with the actual restriction $C_B$ of [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], retaining underlying abelian sheaves and maps, not merely an unspecified equivalence. Both functors are additive. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] both preserve limits and colimits, hence kernels and cokernels, so they are exact. In particular their termwise extensions identify cohomology (kernels modulo images), preserve and reflect acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms, and commute with arbitrary direct sums. These assertions require neither points nor a terminal object.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; constant-ring specialization; categories.tex Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact

proof.text: Put $T=C_BM\otimes_B C_BN$. Its pure-tensor pairing, valued in the underlying sheaf of $E(T)$, is a restriction-compatible $B^{\mathrm{pre}}$-bilinear pairing. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] with $\mathcal O=B^{\mathrm{pre}}$. The module sheafifications of the restricted $M,N$ identify with $M,N$ by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] (their underlying abelian sheaves are already sheaves, and the counit is the identity on original sections). Thus this pairing is $R$-bilinear on $M\times N$. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] it gives $M\otimes_RN\to E(T)$ sending $m\otimes_R n$ to $m\otimes_B n$. Conversely the pairing $m,n\mapsto m\otimes_R n$ is $B$-bilinear, so the sheafified objectwise tensor universal property [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators], with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_B$, gives $T\to C_B(M\otimes_RN)$. Both composites fix every pure tensor; the same two universal properties show that they are identities. They are therefore inverse isomorphisms. Applying morphisms $a,b$ sends every such tensor to $a(m)\otimes b(n)$ in either construction; uniqueness proves naturality in both variables.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor and its bilinear-map hint; Tag 03CY

proof.text:
For the unit, $C_B\dashv E$ (step 1) gives $\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_BR,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,E H)$. Precomposition with $\iota$ maps this bijectively onto $\operatorname{Hom}_{B^{\mathrm{pre}}}(B^{\mathrm{pre}},E H)$: an $R$-linear $f$ satisfies $f_U(r)=r\,f_U(1)$ and $1=\iota_U(1)$, so $f$ is determined by $f\iota$; conversely a $B$-linear natural $g$ gives the restriction-compatible family $n_U=g_U(1)$ (restrictions of $B^{\mathrm{pre}}$ are identities), and $f_U(r)=r\,n_U$ is natural, $R$-linear and satisfies $f\iota=g$ because $B$ acts on $EH$ through $\iota$. Thus $R$ with $\iota$ is the module sheafification of $B^{\mathrm{pre}}$ in the sense of [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], whose underlying abelian sheaf is the abelian sheafification.
The set $\operatorname{Hom}_{B^{\mathrm{pre}}}(B^{\mathrm{pre}},E H)$ consists of the restriction-compatible $B$-linear maps from the constant module presheaf to $H$. Hence $C_BR$, with $b\mapsto\iota(b)$, is its sheafification. Uniqueness of sheafification identifies it with the tensor unit of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], fixing the image of each $b$. Check the constraints by precomposing with pure tensors, using the equality-detection bijections of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and [lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators] repeatedly. The associator diagram on $(m\otimes n)\otimes l$ gives $m\otimes(n\otimes l)$ on both paths; the symmetry diagram gives $n\otimes m$; the left and right unitor diagrams on $b\otimes m$ and $m\otimes b$ both give $\iota(b)m=bm$. Thus the comparison is symmetric monoidal. The inverse equivalence gets the inverse comparisons, with the same identities.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 0GMW; Section 03EK, tensor constraints and bilinear universal property

proof.text:
Apply the ordinary comparison on each $(p,q)$ summand and the direct-sum comparison from step 1. In total degree $n$ this gives
$C_B(\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_RQ^q)\cong\bigoplus_{p+q=n}C_BP^p\otimes_B C_BQ^q$.
Naturality with $d_P$ and $d_Q$ identifies the two parts $d_P\otimes1$ and $1\otimes d_Q$ of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]; additivity preserves the coefficient $(-1)^p$. These degreewise isomorphisms therefore form a natural chain isomorphism of signed direct-sum totals. Their inverses give the analogous comparison for $E$. The associator and unit diagrams agree on each direct-sum injection by step 3; the symmetry sends a homogeneous tensor to $(-1)^{pq}$ times the reversed tensor on both paths. This proves coherence for the total-complex comparisons, including all signs.

source.place: Section 06YL, total tensor convention; homology.tex Definition 012Z

proof.text:
For a fixed module sheaf $M$, step 2 identifies tensor with $C_BM$ with the conjugate by $C_B,E$ of tensor with $M$. Since these equivalences are exact and essentially surjective, one tensor functor is exact if and only if the other is. This proves preservation and reflection of flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For a complex $P$ and any acyclic fixed-$B$ complex $A$, step 1 makes $EA$ acyclic and step 4 identifies
$C_B\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R EA)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(C_BP\otimes_B A)$.
Acyclicity on one side is equivalent to that on the other. Every acyclic complex on either side is obtained this way, up to the termwise equivalence isomorphism. This proves preservation and reflection of K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The symmetric total braiding gives the same assertion with the two tensor arguments interchanged.

For completeness, the acyclic-test definition equals the quasi-isomorphism-test definition [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. On $R$-module complexes, tensoring a cone is the cone of the tensor map by [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso], while a map is a quasi-isomorphism precisely when its cone is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Thus an acyclic-test K-flat complex tensors every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism. Conversely apply quasi-isomorphism preservation to $0\to A$ for an arbitrary acyclic $A$; its tensor source is zero, so its tensor target is acyclic. Symmetry handles the other side. Steps 1 and 4 transfer this equivalence to fixed-$B$ complexes: lift any complex or map by $E$, and use preservation and reflection of acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms.

Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to $C_B$ and $E$, exact by step 1. The termwise unit and counit isomorphisms descend through localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Their inverse identities remain identities after localization. Hence $D(C_B)$ and $D(E)$ are mutually inverse equivalences on the ordinary unbounded derived categories, with their specified termwise localization comparisons.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; Tag 05RT and definition of the derived category

proof.text:
Use the full subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of K-flat complexes with flat terms in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Steps 1 and 5 identify it under the homotopy-category equivalence with the corresponding subcategory $\mathcal P_B$, and identify their quasi-isomorphisms. Thus its resolving localization equivalence transports to $W_B^{-1}\mathcal P_B\simeq D(\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B))$. On $P,Q\in\mathcal P_R$, the chain isomorphism of step 4 yields
$D(C_B)(QP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QQ)\cong D(C_B)(QP)\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}D(C_B)(QQ)$
under the canonical total-tensor localization comparisons. Its naturality commutes with every quasi-isomorphism in either variable, so the uniqueness and extension assertion of the cited descent node, transported through the equivalence in step 7, extends it to all derived objects and morphisms. Inverting the chain comparison supplies its inverse. On three resolving arguments the two associativity paths agree by step 4; successively localizing each variable proves the derived associator equation. The same argument with two variables proves symmetry, and with the flat regular unit in degree zero proves both unitor equations. Hence these are the coherent comparisons computed by the stated total maps on corresponding K-flat resolutions. Any K-flat representatives may be used: by step 6 tensor with them preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so comparison with flat-term K-flat resolutions gives the same localized maps.
